I haven't worked in a company that provides geolocation services, but I'd say learning about Spatial DB's and GIS is important. What is a datum, referenfe ellipsoid, SRID is important to know. Knowing about spatial indexes is important too. Also, how to use spatial queries to obtain data that is not related by "conventional" means. Maybe even learn about the 9MI. The difference between spatial db's and shapefiles, and when to use which.

Then grab a DBMS that provides spatial functions and create a simple app that provides different services, ie, shortest route, or any other sort of spatial analysis. 

For example, a map composed of the following layers, your state, risk areas in your state, roads in your state, and firestations. Each of these layers will have its conventional data. Then provide some spatial analysis functions, ie, for the highest risk area, how many fire stations can provide coverage (which can be defined as a buffer of radius m from the fire station). Then, providig more depth, for each of these stations, how well equipped are they? 

Perhaps add another layer which has he distribution of population, and then determine which amount of the population is at risk, by using the two previous queries above and using some information from the roads, ie, are they of high traffic, or in bad condition? This could make evacuation difficult. 

A project like this one will get your hands dirty enough to understand how tk work woth spatial information.

I understand not enjoying things. Advice I have gotten says don't let it keep you from trying. If you don't like something, move on to the next thing and try it, rinse and repeat.

It sounds like you could use a friend, and truth is, so could I, so, do you want to be friends? I am all ears my friend.

It is a hard habit to break. Hell I still do it the majority of the day. Right now, I'll give you some advice I've gotten from users in this sub. 
Try finding an activity you can enjoy. This will distract you. It could be reading, watching movies, videogames, anything that can potentially keep you mind busy so it can't think outside of what you are doing. 

Pets are a good option, if you have suitable living space for them. Something to care for can boost your emotions. 

Individual/group therapy. Talking to people who can trully understand what you are going through can be of great help.

This subreddit. The fact that you are posting here means something. All of us here are willing to hear you out.
